text:
Alexandre Texier's role grew the week Ivan Demidov went down. He's up to about 14 minutes a night from under 11, and he's one of the forwards Montreal is leaning on while its injury list grows. The France international, in his second season with the Canadiens after stops in Columbus and St. Louis, has five points in 20 games.

The scoring is the weak part, 2 goals on 4.0 expected and only one goal in his last ten games, but the rest of his game has been better than the line suggests. Montreal takes 57% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, 8 points better than without him, and he's taking more dangerous shots than he did last season (0.88 expected goals per 60 against 0.62). The team has also scored about three fewer goals than expected during his shifts.

Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season against tough competition, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking doesn't find a standout strength or weakness. Our talent range has him around 14 goals. For a depth winger on a team whose results are running ahead of its play, he's quietly one of the forwards on the right side of the chances.
